Container.Name: bfbackup-controller
Container.Overview: BFBackup controller: web UI, schedules and database. Backs up folders incrementally and fast over the LAN to other servers (running the bfbackup-peer container), to local disks or to USB drives. Backups are plain files and folders on the target: no repository, no archive format, you can open and copy them without BFBackup. You need one controller and, for backups to other servers, one bfbackup-peer per server. Peers connect to port 7701 with a token you create in the web UI. Made for Unraid, works on any Linux Docker host.
Container.Changes: See https://github.com/delsol-ger/bfbackup/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md. Each release says whether the peers need the update too.
Container.Requires: For backups to another server, install bfbackup-peer there.

Config.Name: Web UI port
Config.Description: Web interface. Keep it in your LAN or VPN, never forward it to the internet.

Config.Name: Peer port
Config.Description: Peers connect here. Must be reachable from every peer.

Config.Name: Storage
Config.Description: Keep /mnt on both sides. It covers all shares and USB drives, and lets deleted files be moved to the trash instead of copied. Do not narrow this path to restrict access: use 'Allowed roots' below instead.

Config.Name: Allowed roots
Config.Description: Restrict access here, not in 'Storage'. Comma-separated folders BFBackup may read and write; nothing outside is reachable. /mnt = everything. USB drives are only found if /mnt/disks is listed too. Example: /mnt/user/Backups,/mnt/disks (one share plus USB drives).

Config.Name: Owner UID for written files
Config.Description: Files and folders BFBackup creates get this owner (99 = nobody on Unraid). Empty: leave as root.

Config.Name: Peer transport
Config.Description: auto: accept encrypted and unencrypted peers (older versions, BFB_TRANSPORT=plain). tls: refuse unencrypted peers.
